_rules: This file is the queue. Published state lives on disk: a topic is consumed when a posts/*-<slug>.md file exists. No status fields — delete a post file to re-open its topic.

Rotation: the next pick must differ in `type` from the most recently published post. Four types cycle: question (first-person long tail), fact-world (the product in text), definition (category/GEO terms), comparison (the commercial SERP Calm and Headspace abandoned).
`python3 build.py next` applies both rules and scaffolds the pick. Written at brief time, not publish time.

Fact-worlds are the plurality and should stay so. Verified 2026-09-01: they are the only type that both matches an underserved SERP and IS the product. The category idea is no longer a differentiator — WikiSleep, Nocturn Tales and Slumber Studios all ship it. The specific material is.
Order is winnability, not theme. The list is interleaved by type on purpose so the rotation rule preserves the intended order instead of silently resequencing it.
Any post asserting a year, a percentage or a measurement needs 2+ `sources:` URLs in its frontmatter, or the build hard-fails. Check the claim before citing; do not staple on a plausible link.

Do NOT chase: how to fall asleep fast, can't sleep, sleep hygiene, deep sleep, sleep quality, insomnia, sleepmaxxing, bare 'sleep stories', 'cognitive shuffling'. Those SERPs are Cleveland Clinic / Mayo / NHS / CDC, and the page type that wins there needs claims this site will not make.

Never write the bare two-word phrase 'low arousal' in a title, H1 or the App Store description — it is a Wikipedia-backed clinical term (the Low Arousal Approach, McDonnell 1994) and in psychology low arousal IMPAIRS learning. Only the hyphenated three-word 'low-arousal learning' is ours.
Add topics at the bottom. Never reuse a slug. If a topic stops making sense, delete the row — the file is the decision log via git.
